answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying influence to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to account creation. Each agent accumulates a reputation signal only by completing attested tasks whose results peers can check, and that signal decays whenever the agent goes idle, so influence must be continuously earned. A fresh identity starts at zero and cannot wander into high-trust roles, while onyx-hard audit logs make past behaviour permanent and checkable. Spinning up a thousand fake agents buys nothing: each must do real, costly work for weeks before it can sway anything.
